name: Net Present Value of a Cash-Flow List
description: Discounts a whole list of cash flows at rate r and adds them up; the first value is at time 0 (not discounted), the next one period later, and so on.
notes: Same convention as the textbook NPV. Spreadsheet NPV() assumes the first value is one period away, so add the time-0 flow separately there.

name: Internal Rate of Return of a Cash-Flow List
description: Finds the discount rate that makes the NPV of the cash flows zero.
notes: Assumes one sign change for a unique answer; with several sign changes there can be more than one IRR. Shown as a fraction (0.16 = 16 %).

name: Modified Internal Rate of Return
description: Computes the MIRR: negative flows are discounted at the finance rate, positive flows compounded to the end at the reinvestment rate, and the rate linking the two is returned.
notes: Avoids the multiple-answer problem of IRR and the unrealistic assumption that proceeds are reinvested at the IRR itself.

name: Discounted Payback Period
expression: sum(k, 1, len(cf) - 1, sum(j, 0, k - 1, at(cf, j + 1) / (1 + r)^j) < 0)
description: Counts the whole periods before the cumulative discounted cash flow turns non-negative.
notes: Unlike the simple payback period it respects the time value of money. Returns the number of periods still under water; the investment pays back during the next one.

name: Present Value of Uneven Cash Flows

variables.label: Cash flows at the end of periods 1, 2, …

description: Discounts a list of future cash flows, the first one period from now, back to today.
notes: This is what spreadsheet NPV(rate; values) computes.

name: Future Value of Uneven Cash Flows
expression: sum(k, 1, len(cf), at(cf, k) * (1 + r)^(len(cf) - k))

variables.label: Deposits at the end of periods 1, 2, …

description: Compounds a list of end-of-period deposits forward to the end of the last period.
notes: The last deposit earns no interest; the first earns n − 1 periods of it.

name: Number of Periods to Reach a Future Value
description: Solves FV = PV(1 + r)^n for the number of periods n.
notes: At 7 % money doubles in about 10.24 periods (the rule of 72 gives 10.3).

name: Required Rate to Reach a Future Value
description: Solves FV = PV(1 + r)^n for the rate r.
notes: Doubling in 10 years needs about 7.18 % a year.

name: Number of Payments to Pay Off a Loan
description: Solves the annuity formula for the number of level payments needed to repay a loan.
notes: The payment must exceed the interest r·PV, otherwise the loan is never repaid. Here about 41.0 payments.

name: Number of Deposits to Reach a Savings Goal
expression: ln(1 + fv * r / pmt) / ln(1 + r)
description: Solves the future value of an ordinary annuity for the number of deposits.
notes: Saving 500 a month at 0.5 % a month reaches 100,000 after about 139 deposits.

name: Rate of an Annuity (Solve for r)
description: Finds the periodic interest rate implied by a loan amount, payment and term — what spreadsheet RATE() computes — by solving the annuity equation numerically.
notes: Multiply by 12 for a nominal annual rate on monthly payments. Here about 0.0088 per period.

name: Level Payment for a Future Value (Annuity Due)
description: Gives the deposit, made at the start of each period, needed to accumulate a target amount.
notes: Paying in advance needs slightly less than end-of-period saving (the sinking fund payment).

name: Present Value of a Growing Perpetuity Due
description: Values an infinite stream of payments growing at g, with the first paid immediately.
notes: Requires r > g.

name: Present Value of a Deferred Annuity
description: Values n level payments that start only after d periods (the first payment at the end of period d + 1).
notes: Used for pensions that start at retirement and for education savings.

name: Present Value of an Annuity with Continuous Discounting
description: Values n end-of-period payments when interest is compounded continuously at force δ (per period).
notes: Equivalent to the ordinary annuity with r = e^δ − 1.

name: Present Value of a Continuous Income Stream
description: Values income received continuously at a constant rate for t years, discounted at force δ: ∫₀ᵗ c e^(−δs) ds.
notes: The continuous analogue of an annuity, used for rents and royalties modelled as flows.

name: Force of Interest from an Effective Rate
description: Converts an effective annual rate to the equivalent continuously compounded rate (force of interest) δ = ln(1 + i).
notes: 5 % effective equals about 4.879 % continuous.

name: Nominal Rate from an Effective Rate
description: Converts an effective annual rate to the nominal annual rate compounded m times a year.
notes: An effective 5 % equals about 4.889 % nominal compounded monthly.

name: Equivalent Periodic Rate
description: Gives the rate per sub-period (e.g. per month) that compounds to the effective annual rate.
notes: 6 % a year is about 0.4868 % a month, slightly less than 6 %/12 = 0.5 %.

name: Discount Rate from Interest Rate (d = i/(1+i))
description: Converts an interest rate (charged at the end) to the equivalent discount rate (deducted up front): d = i/(1 + i).
notes: 5 % interest equals about 4.762 % discount. Treasury bills and actuarial tables use discount rates.

name: Rule of 114 (Tripling Time)
description: Estimates the time for money to triple at pct percent a year as 114/pct.
notes: At 8 % money triples in about 14.3 years (exactly 14.27).

name: Present Value with Different Rates per Period
expression: sum(k, 1, len(cf), at(cf, k) / prod(j, 1, k, 1 + at(rt, j)))
description: Discounts each cash flow through the rates of all periods before it, for a changing interest-rate path.
notes: With a yield curve use forward rates here.

name: Present Value of a Perpetuity with Payments Every k Periods
description: Values an infinite series of payments made every k periods, the first after k periods.
notes: Useful for costs that recur every few years, such as replacing a roof.

name: Capitalised Cost
description: Gives the present value of owning something forever: first cost plus the perpetuity of its annual cost.
notes: Used in engineering economy to compare long-lived public projects.

name: Arithmetic Gradient Present Worth
description: Values a cash flow that is 0 at period 1 and rises by G each period (G, 2G, … at periods 2, 3, …): the (P/G, i, n) factor.
notes: Add the ordinary annuity for the base amount to value a series such as 1000, 1100, 1200 and so on.

name: Arithmetic Gradient Uniform Series
description: Converts an arithmetic gradient G into the equivalent level payment per period: the (A/G, i, n) factor.
notes: For G = 100 over 10 periods at 6 % the level equivalent is about 402.2.
